country.comment: Survey conducted in three municipalities across three districts and physiographic regions of Nepal: Tinpatan Rural Municipality (Sindhuli), Badigad Rural Municipality (Baglung), and Chandannath Municipality (Jumla).

effect_estimate.comment: Linear regressions (Tables 5 and 6) test only climate-hazard predictors against source depletion, drying up, and turbidity; institutional, community-management, and O&M fund-collection variables are reported descriptively via FIETS component scores and tap-stand functionality percentages without regression estimates linking governance variables to WASH outcomes.
effect_estimate.value: Across 103 community-managed WASH systems (3,896 tap-stands; 338 water sources), only 32% of tap-stands were fully functional, 62% partially functional, and 6% non-functional; 63% of water sources were depleted and 5% dried up; 72% of households had permanent toilets, 20% shared toilets, and 8% practiced open defecation. On the FIETS sustainability index (0-100%), systems averaged 70% on Financial (WUSC O&M fund collection and management), 50% on Institutional, 41% on Environmental, 67% on Technical, and 70% on Social components, with 0% achieving good (>90%), 3% satisfactory (76-90%), 74% average (51-75%), and 23% low (<=50%) sustainability. In linear regressions of perceived hazards on WASH impacts (n = 103), drought predicted source depletion (beta = 0.84, R2 = 0.71, F = 243, p < 0.005), source drying up (beta = 0.65, R2 = 0.42, F = 72, p < 0.005), and water quality deterioration (beta = 0.55, R2 = 0.30, F = 44, p < 0.005), while landslides (beta = 0.69, R2 = 0.48, F = 93, p < 0.005) and floods (beta = 0.58, R2 = 0.33, F = 51, p < 0.005) predicted water quality deterioration.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 9-11, Sections 3.4.1 & 3.4.2; Tables 5 & 6, PDF pp. 9-10; Figure 5, PDF p. 11

mechanism_certainty.comment: Cross-sectional survey (ceiling 2) documenting descriptive FIETS component scores for WUSC O&M fund management (70%) and institutional capacity (50%) alongside system functionality and disruption attributions (lack of timely maintenance, reckless local road construction), without directly observing legal/administrative procedures operating on access or estimating statistical regressions for institutional predictors.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 6, Section 2.3.4; PDF pp. 10-11, Sections 3.4.1 & 3.4.2; Figure 5, PDF p. 11

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines community-managed WASH governance via Water Users and Sanitation Committees (WUSCs) and community engagement (participation), WUSC-level operation and maintenance fund collection and management (fees), and weak institutional governance capacity (50% FIETS score) alongside uncoordinated local road construction damaging water infrastructure (institutional_fragmentation).
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 2, Section 1; PDF p. 6, Section 2.3.4; PDF pp. 10-11, Sections 3.4.1 & 3.4.2

sample_size.comment: 103 community-managed WASH systems sampled out of 138 systems constructed in 2011-2021 across 3 municipalities (53 in Tinpatan RM, 27 in Badigad RM, 23 in Chandannath Municipality), covering 3,896 tap-stands and 338 water sources, with surveys administered to 103 WUSC representatives and 103 caretakers (note Table 3 sex breakdown sums to 102 WUSC respondents [91 male + 11 female] though municipality totals sum to 103), supplemented by 1994-2024 meteorological records from 5 DHM stations.
sample_size.value: 103 community-managed WASH systems (3,896 tap-stands; 338 water sources) across 3 municipalities; 206 survey respondents (103 Water Users and Sanitation Committee [WUSC] members and 103 caretakers)

study_design.comment: Cross-sectional structured/semi-structured questionnaire survey conducted in January-February 2024 across purposively selected physiographic regions and randomly sampled WASH systems, analyzed via descriptive statistics, OLS linear regression, FIETS sustainability scoring, and 30-year meteorological trend validation.
study_design.value: Quantitative cross-sectional questionnaire survey with linear regression, FIETS sustainability index scoring, and historical meteorological time-series trend analysis (1994-2024)
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 2, Section 2; PDF pp. 4-6, Sections 2.2-2.4
